sources.entry: Python: _ugit: Learn Git Internals by Building Git Yourself_

summary.title: Git Internals by Nikita Leshenko
summary.one_liner: You learn how Git works internally by implementing a small Git-like version control system, μgit (ugit), in Python one incremental code change at a time.
keywords: understanding git rebase and force push
takeaways: Git's core ideas (commits, branches, index, merges, remotes) can be understood by implementing a simplified version of them.
ugit is built as a series of code changes, each with an explanation and a diff, so you can follow along step by step.
ugit omits object compression, file modes and commit timestamps to keep the code short, while keeping the essential Git concepts.
A working knowledge of everyday Git commands (commit, branch, merge, push, pull) is a prerequisite; the tutorial is not an introduction to using Git.
Install ugit in development mode with python3 setup.py develop --user to run and edit the code while following along.
summary.summary: The page introduces μgit (ugit), a small Git-like version control system written in Python, and presents it as a tutorial organized into incremental code changes. Each change includes an explanation and a diff, starting from a minimal "hello world" application with a setup.py that defines the executable. The author argues that understanding Git internals helps with collaboration problems such as rebase and force push, and that seeing concepts in running code aids understanding more than diagrams or the production C source. The tutorial is aimed at readers who already know Git's everyday commands.
